bug_semantics: Unauthenticated stored XSS via utm_campaign in WP Statistics visitor/referral admin reports. An attacker POSTs to the public REST route /wp-statistics/v2/hit using the request signature that Helper::getHitsDefaultParams() localizes onto the public homepage. The required page_uri POST body is base64 and is applied by Hits::set_page_uri() and Helper::getRequestUri(), which decode it without sanitize_url() and therefore override the already-sanitized REQUEST_URI. Pages::get_page_type() always includes a search_query key, so sanitize_page_uri() never strips the query string; FilterQueryStringUrl() then keeps utm_campaign because it is on the default allow-list. The stored pages.uri query is later extracted by Url::getParam() into campaign labels and page-query tooltips (class wps-tooltip). Those titles use esc_attr/esc_html, but admin tooltipster is initialized with contentAsHTML:true, so the browser-decoded title is inserted as HTML when an administrator opens Visitors or Referred Visitors. Injection-pattern checks on the hit request block
flaw_origin: e83c5a764428a95c1e04fc9d67160c2bbde3e223 ('pref : add Coming Soon to the CSV Metrics button') is the smallest first-write of the execution sink. To render an italic phrase in a Metrics CSV tooltip it globally set tooltipster contentAsHTML:true on every .wps-tooltip, including visitor-report campaign labels that already carried stored utm_campaign values. The immediate parent still initializes tooltipster with only contentCloning:true (default contentAsHTML:false), so the same esc_attr titles were text. Prerequisite unsanitized REST page_uri decode was written earlier (Hits::set_page_uri in 34007de740dfe18ff11645f10f92041e5ed91ab4; Helper::getRequestUri in 1855e2916c1fd2a06a00eb8b3047777c2d04900d) and the campaign labels themselves in b6a63937125822eb8b54a0608354733596e881fd / 92c9641d16c5137cf482fb6ac9e8a111a46b7e05; those commits are necessary storage/display but did not yet interpret the title as HTML.

Advisory attack path: plant via POST /wp-statistics/v2/hit because the signature is on the public homepage and base64 page_uri overrides sanitized REQUEST_URI so malicious utm_campaign is stored. First-party fix ref https://github.com/wp-statistics/wp-statistics/commit/6ab74427778b89c9e88471e9dd7407d9055a9b34. Wordfence also cites helper.js#L267 (wps_js.tooltip), class-wp-statistics-helper.php#L1462, class-wp-statistics-hits.php#L102, referred-visitors.php#L79, visitors.php#L94, class-wp-statistics-api-hit.php#L78 on tags 14.16.7 and 14.16.8.

v14.16.8 Helper::getRequestUri() (includes/class-wp-statistics-helper.php:1462-1468): REST + isset($_REQUEST['page_uri']) returns base64_decode($_REQUEST['page_uri']) with no sanitize_url; non-REST path uses sanitize_url(wp_unslash($_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'])). v14.16.8 Hits::set_page_uri() (includes/class-wp-statistics-hits.php:102-104): return isset($this->rest_hits->page_uri) ? base64_decode($this->rest_hits->page_uri) : $page_uri. Hit::hit_callback() at includes/api/v2/class-wp-statistics-api-hit.php:78 calls Helper::validateHitRequest() then Hits::record(); permission_callback is checkSignature only.

Helper::getHitsDefaultParams() localizes signature = Signature::generate([source_type, source_id]) when request signatures are enabled, so the homepage tracker object supplies the unauthenticated REST hit HMAC. validateHitRequest() injectionPatterns() reject <script> and quoted on* attributes but not unquoted handlers.

Pages::get_page_type() default array always has search_query => '', so sanitize_page_uri()'s explode('?') strip (gated on array_key_exists('search_query') === false) never runs. FilterQueryStringUrl then keeps allow-listed params. includes/defines/query-params-allow-list.php default list includes utm_campaign. Visitor::get_page_by_id() sets params['query'] = Url::getParams(home_url() . uri).

v14.16.8 views/components/tables/visitors.php:89-94 and referred-visitors.php:74-79: Url::getParam('?' . $page['query'], 'utm_campaign') is written into span.wps-campaign-label.wps-tooltip title with esc_attr/esc_html; the sibling internal-link tooltip is '?' . $page['query'] via views/components/objects/internal-link.php (esc_attr). Campaign labels first written in b6a63937125822eb8b54a0608354733596e881fd (2025-08-20, visitors/top/most-active) and 92c9641d16c5137cf482fb6ac9e8a111a46b7e05 (2025-08-24, referred/latest-referrals); first tag v14.15.4.

git log -S contentAsHTML -- assets/dev/javascript/helper.js yields only e83c5a764428a95c1e04fc9d67160c2bbde3e223 (2025-10-14, Nora , single parent 17880ba9257556b1e6e1193755654acfa719eabb). Diff adds contentAsHTML: true to both tooltipster inits in wps_js.tooltip (helper.js lines 267-278 on 14.16.8). Parent helper.js tooltipster options are only theme + contentCloning:true. Parent assets/js/admin.min.js has no contentAsHTML:!0; the BIC compiled bundle does. Same commit puts HTML ('At a glance') into the Metrics CSV title unescaped, which is why HTML mode was enabled globally.

Parent-tree verification at 17880ba9257556b1e6e1193755654acfa719eabb: visitors.php already has the utm_campaign wps-tooltip label; Helper::getRequestUri still returns raw base64_decode($_REQUEST['page_uri']); contentAsHTML is absent. Therefore the HTML execution sink is first written on the BIC, not inherited.

reasoning: CVE-2026-15780 / GHSA-3hm7-m5p9-2h77 is a real, published Wordfence CNA record (not withdrawn). The complete stored-XSS lifecycle is: (1) REST hit accepts client page_uri; (2) decode without sanitize_url overrides the sanitized REQUEST_URI so allow-listed utm_campaign is stored on pages.uri; (3) visitor/referral tables extract that value into .wps-tooltip titles; (4) admin tooltipster with contentAsHTML:true executes it. Step 4 is the first time the stored campaign is an HTML sink. git log -L on getRequestUri and -S on base64_decode($this->rest_hits->page_uri) show the storage gap was written in 2022-2023, and the campaign labels in August 2025 already used esc_attr/esc_html, which is sufficient while tooltipster defaults to text. The smallest commit that first wrote the vulnerable execution lines is therefore e83c5a764428a95c1e04fc9d67160c2bbde3e223, which added contentAsHTML:true to wps_js.tooltip (the helper.js#L267 function Wordfence cited) so a Coming Soon Metrics CSV tooltip could include <i> markup. Parent 17880ba9257556b1e6e1193755654acfa719eabb was checked directly: campaign labels and unsanitized page_uri decode are already present, contentAsHTML is not, and admin.min.js lacks contentAsHTML:!0. The commit is a single-parent first-write, not a squash/move. It is in v14.16 through v14.16.8, i.e. inside the disclosed affected window, and the 14.16.9 squash 4a912c6e9080a1f0148b1a4b7dc921557b464c8e lands sanitize_url on both decode sites plus sanitize_text_field on every campaign label (direct member 6ab74427778b89c9e88471e9dd7407d9055a9b34, the advisory URL). Wordfence's 'all versions <= 14.16.8' lower bound is broader than the HTML-sink introduction; the BIC still precedes the patched 14.16.9 boundary. AI is judged only from that BIC commit object: human author/committer Nora <mwdrad@gmail.com>, no AI trailers, so NOT_AI.
